sections.title: Warm-up
sections.prompt: Say one thing that plays an important role in your work, and one decision you took into account.
items: Diese Entscheidung spielt eine wichtige Rolle.
sections.lede: Say each line aloud once. This section is not scored.

sections.title: Learning objectives
sections.lede: These are the three things you will be able to do by the end of the lesson.

sections.title: The big picture
sections.lede: Collocations are the words that naturally go together; idioms are fixed expressions whose meaning is not literal.

blocks.text: A collocation is a habitual pairing: eine Rolle spielen, eine Entscheidung treffen, zur Verfügung stehen. The individual words are simple, but the combination is what sounds natural. Learning nouns with their verbs is more useful than learning either alone.

Idioms are fixed phrases such as “ins Auge fallen” (to stand out) or “in Kauf nehmen” (to accept a drawback). Use them sparingly and only when the register fits. A misplaced idiom sounds worse than a plain sentence.

blocks.title: Learn the whole chunk
blocks.text: Do not translate “take a decision” word by word. Learn “eine Entscheidung treffen” as one unit and reuse it.

sections.title: Rules & patterns
sections.lede: The patterns to keep in mind while you work through the examples.

rows: Diese Entscheidung spielt eine wichtige Rolle.
Wir nehmen längere Wartezeiten in Kauf.
Der Raum steht allen zur Verfügung.
Der Fehler fällt sofort ins Auge.

items: Use “treffen” with Entscheidung, but “machen” with Fehler.
“Zur Verfügung stehen” takes the dative: mir zur Verfügung stehen.
Idioms are usually informal or journalistic; avoid them in formal reports.

items.de: Der Fehler fällt sofort ins Auge.

items.note: Zur Verfügung stehen takes the dative.

sections.title: Pronunciation
sections.lede: Short, focused sound work. Play each item and repeat it twice.

items.hint: The r is soft and the o is short: ROL-le.
Stress the second word: tsur fer-FOO-gung.
The au sounds like “ow”: ins OW-ge fal-len.

blocks.text: German business language uses collocations more than idioms. “Eine Entscheidung treffen” and “zur Verfügung stellen” appear in almost every formal email.
Idioms such as “ins Fettnäpfchen treten” (to put your foot in it) belong to informal conversation. Using them correctly can build rapport, but they are risky in writing.

sections.title: Dialogue in context
sections.lede: Read the scene, then play it and follow the speakers.
sections.setting: Two colleagues discuss a decision about a new office.

lines.speaker: Kollegin
lines.de: Welche Rolle spielt der Preis bei der Entscheidung?
lines.en: What role does the price play in the decision?

lines.speaker: Kollege
lines.de: Der Preis ist wichtig, aber die Lage fällt stärker ins Auge.
lines.en: The price is important, but the location stands out more.

lines.speaker: Kollegin
lines.de: Dann nehmen wir längere Wege in Kauf?

lines.speaker: Kollege
lines.de: Ja, wenn uns mehr Räume zur Verfügung stehen.
lines.en: Yes, if more rooms are available to us.

sections.title: Grammar spotlight
sections.heading: Collocations in context
sections.lede: Learn the noun with its verb and preposition.

blocks.text: A dictionary entry is useful only if it shows the collocation. Note “eine Entscheidung treffen”, not just “Entscheidung = decision”.

sections.tip: Collect five collocations per week in full sentences. A chunk you can say is worth more than a list you can only recognise.

sections.title: Listening
sections.lede: Listen twice before you look at the transcript.
sections.speaker: Ein Gespräch über eine Stellenanzeige

script.speaker: Bewerberin
script.de: Welche Rolle spielt die Erfahrung für die Stelle?
script.en: What role does experience play for the position?

script.speaker: Personal
script.de: Eine große Rolle. Aber auch die Motivation fällt ins Auge.
script.en: A big role. But motivation also stands out.

script.speaker: Bewerberin
script.de: Würden Sie auch eine längere Einarbeitung in Kauf nehmen?
script.en: Would you also accept a longer training period?

script.speaker: Personal
script.de: Ja, wenn uns dafür mehr Zeit zur Verfügung steht.
script.en: Yes, if we have more time available for it.

questions.prompt: What plays a big role according to the HR manager?
questions.explanation: The HR manager says experience plays a big role.

questions.prompt: What does the applicant ask about?
questions.explanation: The applicant asks about accepting a longer training period.

sections.title: Speaking
sections.lede: Record or say your answer aloud, then compare it with the model.
sections.prompt: Use three collocations to describe a recent decision at work or in study.

model.de: Bei meiner letzten Entscheidung spielte die Zeit eine wichtige Rolle. Wir haben längere Wege in Kauf genommen, weil uns mehr Räume zur Verfügung standen. Der Unterschied fiel sofort ins Auge.
model.en: In my last decision, time played an important role. We accepted longer journeys because more rooms were available to us. The difference stood out immediately.

tips: Say the whole collocation, not just the noun.
Use one idiom at most in a short answer.
Check the preposition: zur Verfügung, ins Auge, in Kauf.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.lede: These are the errors learners most often make with this pattern.

items.wrong: Der Raum steht allen zur verfügung.
items.right: Der Raum steht allen zur Verfügung.
items.why: Verfügung is a noun and must be capitalised.

items.wrong: Wir nehmen längere Wartezeiten auf Kauf.
items.right: Wir nehmen längere Wartezeiten in Kauf.
items.why: The fixed expression is in Kauf nehmen.
